title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of employers' organizations

description.narrative:
The Chinese Employers Confederation (CEC) is the leading national organization representing the interests, voice, and position of Employers in China. It engaged in policy advocacy on behalf of members as well as provision of services and assistance.
In 2024 – 2025, CEC has prioritized an effort to enhance its policy work and services around responsible business conduct, with an intent to develop tailored services for member companies that are multinationals. This prioritization follows conclusion of the ILO’s Responsible Supply Chains in Asia (RSCA) Programme in 2022 and reflection on earlier studies conducted in this area, such as the 2017 MOFCOM and UNDP research indicating that Chinese enterprises experience prominent labour relations issues, including problems related to the protection of labour rights and interests. In both the RSCA programme and 2017 research findings indicated that many Chinese enterprises had inadequate knowledge on the core labour standards, responsible business conducts and due diligence. The lack of such knowledge or capacity affected their contribution to social and economic development, as well as enterprise resilience and sustainability.
In 2024/25 the ILO will provide technical and financial assistance to CEC to develop a Guide on labour compliance and responsible business conducts to guide Chinese multinational companies in respecting international labour standards and promote responsible labour practices in their overseas operations. The activity will be reported under CHN179 with primary linkage to P&B Outcome 4.2, with secondary linkage to CHN801. Under secondary linkage, the ILO will provide technical assistance to support CEC in improving capacity to undertake consultation with the private sector and research among members on this topic.
